findings.where: missing; MANIFEST.json gives the reason as no /dev/kvm, QEMU emulation reaching adbd after 113 minutes, "No GTK either, so no desktop build can stand in for a second screen"
findings.what: The two-device frame my row is explicitly to be judged from does not exist. The Android half of the reason is real, but the stated impossibility of a second screen is contradicted by the capture harness itself: 08_state_propagating.json records shots written to three separate directories (08_state_propagating, _b, _c) across two regions in one WebKit run, so two browser contexts side by side could have been composited into a two-device still with no device and no GTK.
findings.why: The one artifact that would show a gesture on one device becoming a sensation on the other in a single frame is absent, and the reason given covers only part of why.

findings.what: The only evidence for state being perceptible without opening the app is a crypto round-trip note: "payload: {\"kind\":\"feeling\",\"from\":\"noor\"} (32 bytes)", "payload carries only ['kind','from']: yes". No rendered notification, lock screen, widget or ambient surface outside the app appears in any of the fourteen present artifacts, and by its own admission the payload cannot name which feeling arrived.
findings.why: The row requires state changes to be perceptible without opening the app; a passing RFC 8291 test is not a perception.

what_is_working: 01_pulse.png shows exactly twelve labelled partner-state signals on one card - MOOD, HERE, PLACE, NEEDS, HAS LEFT, BATTERY, LAST UP, THEIR CLOCK, RINGER, MOVING, SIGNAL, AT HOME - which meets the twelve-signal requirement outright, and 08_state_propagating.mp4 frame 120 shows the same card correctly reduced to the four signals the far device actually reported.

The persistent header strip carrying the partner's line, TRAVELLING, NEED and ENERGY bars is present on every one of 01, 03, 04, 05, 10, 12, 14 and 17 and on every frame of every clip, so partner state genuinely is continuously in view rather than behind a tap.

The feeling objects themselves are real rendered things with baked contact shadows - the spiral, the rubber band, the drawn moon and chair read as objects on a desk, not as icons, and 06_unfolding.mp4 frame 191 shows an authored feeling ("empty chair") carrying its own drawn glyph, which is the right idea even though 15 shows it is not applied consistently.

08_state_propagating.mp4 does demonstrate a real state change crossing the wire: frames 24-40 show the far partner's card go from "nothing from them yet" to "restless / open / nothing / some", and 08_state_propagating.json records link "connected" over http://100.68.254.25:8443/, so propagation is not faked.
verdict: Judged on the evidence alone, the emotional layer is a chat feature wearing paper. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 a feeling crosses the wire and arrives as a note in the transcript reading the word "hold" - a message in a different colour, which is precisely what the row forbids - and the two items that arrive after it never render at all, sitting as flat cream rectangles of RGB (247, 242, 233) with a drop shadow and a luminance standard deviation of 0.98, below the project's own paper floor, for the final 4.5 seconds of the clip. The clip named 07_feeling_landing contains no landing: two sendFeeling steps are logged and the recent-feeling row on Pulse holds the same five objects in the same five positions at frame 0 and frame 383. The picker offers four named families where five are required, spanning x 55 to 1037 of 1080 with no fifth clipped and no scroll cue, with roughly nine tiles and six legible names visible - against a requirement of thirty feelings - and those names are set at 1.95:1 contrast over a translucent wash through which the page beneath collides with them. Authored feelings are visibly second-class: in one frame of 15_authored_feeling.mp4, the built-in "chair" carries a glyph and "sent", "pigeon" carries neither glyph nor delivery, and "tuesday soup" carries no state row at all. The whole capture is WebKit, which means this is the iOS path, and it contains no designed substitute for the missing haptic - only its absence. And no file anywhere under evidence/ records a single haptic pattern, so the central claim of the row, that thirty feelings are each identifiable by touch alone with the screen face down, cannot be checked even once. Four blocking findings stand; the category cannot exceed its floor, and on what is actually visible it falls well short of it.
